pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (devil with scythe)
pairs.question: Unum est solummodo, in quo me superas. Quid est illud?
pairs.answer: Humilitas tua, per quam non praevaleo adversum te.
pairs.derivation: The devil's statement 'Unum est solummodo, in quo me superas' is kept as setup so 'illud' in Macarius's question 'Quid est illud?' has a referent. Dropped the speech tag 'Et dixit abbas:' before the question and 'Cui ille:' before the answer. Answer is the devil's full single-sentence reply.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (sack of sand)
pairs.question: Abba, cur tantum onus portas?
pairs.derivation: Theosebius's interrogative ('cur tantum onus portas') with its full single-sentence reply. Dropped speech tag 'dixit:' before the question and 'Et ille:' before the answer; normalized the rendered '!' to '?'.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (Satan with flasks, first exchange)
pairs.question: Quo vadis?
pairs.derivation: Macarius's question to Satan; reply is the full single sentence. Dropped 'dixit ei:' / 'Et ille:'; normalized rendered '!' to '?'.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (Satan with flasks, why so many)
pairs.question: Quare tot ampullas portas?
pairs.answer: Gustum fratribus porto, et si unum alicui non placebit, offeram aliud vel tertium, et sic per ordinem, ut aliquid placeat.
pairs.derivation: Macarius's interrogative and Satan's reply. Dropped 'Cui Macarius:' / 'Respondit:'; normalized rendered '!' to '?'. Answer kept whole as one sentence directly explaining the flasks.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (Satan with flasks, what did you do)
pairs.question: Quid fecisti?
pairs.answer: Omnes sanctificati sunt et nemo mihi acquievit, nisi unus, qui vocatur Theotistus.
pairs.derivation: Macarius asks on Satan's return; reply is the full single sentence. Dropped 'dixit ei Macarius:' / 'Respondit:'; normalized rendered '!' to '?'. Stopped at the full stop before the narration 'Surgens autem Macarius...'.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (Satan with flasks, second 'quo vadis')
pairs.question: Quo vadis?
pairs.derivation: Macarius's repeated question and Satan's reply. Dropped 'inveniens dixit:' / 'Cui ille:'; normalized rendered '!' to '?'.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (the old man and the devil)
pairs.question: Quid faciunt fratres illi?
pairs.derivation: The senex asks the devil; the one-word reply 'Male' genuinely answers. Dropped 'occurrit senex et dixit:' / 'Cui diabolus:'; normalized rendered '!' to '?'.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (the old man and the devil, why)
pairs.question: Male. Quare?
pairs.answer: Quia omnes sancti sunt et, quod est maius malum, unum, quem habebam, amisi et omnibus sanctior factus est.
pairs.derivation: Kept the devil's prior 'Male' as setup so 'Quare?' has a referent (why 'badly'). Dropped 'Et dixit:' before the question; the answer follows directly with no speech tag. Answer kept whole as the devil's explanatory sentence.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (the pagan skull, where is your soul)
pairs.question: Ubi est anima tua?
pairs.derivation: Macarius asks the skull; reply 'In inferno' answers directly. Dropped 'Et dixit ei Macarius:' / 'Respondit:'; normalized rendered '!' to '?'.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (the pagan skull, deeper souls)
pairs.question: Suntne aliqui te profundiores?
pairs.derivation: Macarius's '-ne' interrogative; reply answers directly. Dropped 'Cui Macarius:' / 'Respondit:'. Sentence-final '?' already present in source.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Historia de Sancto Macario (the pagan skull, beyond the Jews)
pairs.question: Et ultra Iudaeos suntne aliqui profundiores?
pairs.answer: Profundiores omnibus sunt falsi Christiani, qui Christi sanguine redempti tantum pretium parvi pendunt.
pairs.derivation: Macarius's '-ne' interrogative and the skull's full reply. Dropped 'Cui iterum ille:' / 'Cui ille:'; normalized rendered '!' to '?' and dropped trailing whitespace inside the closing quote.
